title: Derived normalization for an ordinary component slice square
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], $W$ a w-contractible affine scheme [sk-def-pe-wlocal], and $U\to W$ a w-contractible affine pro-etale test [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Fix PullbackData $d_W,d_U$, literal profinite RestrictionData $r$, and an OrdinaryComparison $e$ satisfying OrdinaryMonoidal with the fixed schemeCanonicalMonoidal [def-sfb-component-slice-comparison-data]. Then DerivedComparison for these same data and this same ordinary comparison is inhabited. Its four exact derived functors have normalized strong tensor structures; the canonical evaluation comparison obeys the slice and entire derived-section squares; the induced cohomology map is actual pullback on Hom into every integer shift. Fully faithful component pullback on the lower slice implies invertibility of the displayed entire derived-section morphism. No ordinary slice comparison, component data, or uniqueness of ordinary comparisons is constructed by this statement.

proof.text: Exact termwise localization of the four functors gives the specified derivedIso. Compute derived tensors using flat-term K-flat complexes. On each bidegree summand use the ordinary tensor square and its coefficient-unit identity; they descend to the four DerivedMonoidalNormalization equations and the monoidal derived isomorphism.

Slice restriction of derived Hom is normalized by evaluation. Uncurry both composites in evaluation_square and apply the tensorator and monoidal natural-isomorphism equations. Both are the same pulled-back evaluation, so injectivity of transposition proves equality.

Exact evaluation on the two weakly contractible final objects gives the ordinary section comparison with its coefficient-unit formula. Its exact right-derived comparison has the stated homotopy-representative formula. The K-injective Hom-complex model identifies Hom-sections in every integer degree, with the section from the unit mapped to the prescribed transpose. Transposing pulled-back sections and using the unit and shift equations gives cohomology_formula. Apply right-derived sections to evaluation_square, cancel the slice Hom isomorphism, and use naturality of the section comparison to obtain derived_sections_square.

If the lower component functor is fully faithful, all its shifted-Hom maps are bijective, so the local section map is an isomorphism on every cohomology object. Represent it by a map into a K-injective resolution; this map is a quasi-isomorphism and hence inverted by localization. The other factors of the derived section square are invertible, so cancellation gives fully_faithful_test for the displayed global comparison. All constructions are natural and use arbitrary unbounded complexes.

theorem component_slice_derived_normalization
    (W : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine W] [IsWContractibleRing Γ(W, ⊤)]
    (U : W.ProEt) [IsAffine U.left] [IsWContractibleRing Γ(U.left, ⊤)]
    (dW : PullbackData Λ W) (dU : PullbackData Λ U.left)
    (r : RestrictionData Λ (componentMap W U))
    (e : OrdinaryComparison Λ W U dW dU r)
    (he : OrdinaryMonoidal Λ W U dW dU r (schemeCanonicalMonoidal Λ W U) e) :
    Nonempty (DerivedComparison Λ W U dW dU r (schemeCanonicalMonoidal Λ W U) e)
